Chapter 9, verses 30–31

Śrīdhara's commentary: "If you grant liberation only to your devotees and not to those who are not devotees, then do you too show partiality, born of attachment and aversion?" To this he answers no, with the verse beginning "I am the same." I am the same toward all beings; therefore there is no one dear to me and no one hateful to me. Even so, those who worship me with devotion abide in me, and I too abide in them, as the one who bestows grace on them. The point is this: fire removes the pains of darkness, cold, and the like only for those who tend it, and yet it is not partial; so too the <term>kalpavṛkṣa</term> <gloss>the wish-fulfilling tree of heaven</gloss>. In the same way, though I take the side of my devotees, I have no partiality at all; rather, this is the greatness of devotion to me. ॥ 29 ॥

Madhusūdana's commentary: Moreover, such is the greatness of devotion to me that it produces inequality even in one who is impartial. Hear its greatness:

> Even if a man of very wicked conduct worships me with undivided devotion,
> he must be regarded as righteous, for he has resolved rightly. ॥ 30 ॥

Whoever, even if of very wicked conduct, like Ajāmila and others, worships me with undivided devotion, serving me through some dawning of good fortune, he, though formerly unrighteous, must be regarded as righteous. For he has resolved rightly: he possesses a good and firm determination. <note>Ajāmila is the sinful Brahmin of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa who was saved at death by calling out the name of Nārāyaṇa.</note> ॥ 30 ॥

Śrīdhara's commentary: Moreover, showing that the power of devotion to me lies beyond all reasoning, he speaks the verse beginning "Even if." Even a man of extremely wicked conduct, if he does not practise devotion to some other deity separately, but worships me alone, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, must be regarded as righteous, indeed as excellent. For he has resolved rightly: he has made the fine resolve, "Through worship of the Supreme Lord alone I shall reach my goal." ॥ 30 ॥

Madhusūdana's commentary: Through this very right resolve he abandons his wicked conduct, and

> quickly he becomes righteous of soul and attains lasting peace.
> O son of Kuntī, proclaim it: my devotee never perishes. ॥ 31 ॥

Even one who has long been unrighteous of soul, by the greatness of worshipping me, "quickly," that is, very soon, "becomes righteous of soul," his mind following <term>dharma</term> <gloss>righteousness, sacred duty</gloss>. The meaning is that he casts off his wicked conduct at once and becomes a man of good conduct. Further, he "attains lasting," that is, perpetual, "peace," the ceasing of all longing for the enjoyment of sense objects; he attains it fully, through utter dispassion. Someone might say: "Some devotee of yours, not giving up the wicked conduct he practised before, might fail to become righteous of soul, and so he would surely perish." The Lord answers no to this, speaking as if angered, overcome by his compassion for his devotees: Do not think this a marvel, O son of Kuntī; such, beyond doubt, is the greatness of devotion to me. Therefore, even in front of those who dispute it, make the declaration: make the vow with scorn for them and with pride. My devotee, the devotee of me, <term>Vāsudeva</term> <gloss>Krishna, son of Vasudeva</gloss>, even if of extremely wicked conduct, even if fallen into mortal danger, even if, though rarely fit, he is being entreated, even if utterly deluded and without refuge, does not perish; on the contrary, he attains his goal

1 Manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha read "-taḥ śo-." <note>A variant reading in the manuscripts for the words "he has resolved rightly ... the fine resolve" in Śrīdhara's commentary.</note>

<summary>This page of an 1823 Sanskrit edition of the Bhagavad Gītā gives verses 9.30 and 9.31 with the commentaries of Śrīdhara and Madhusūdana Sarasvatī. The commentators explain that God is impartial, yet devotion has such power that even a very wicked person who worships Krishna alone is quickly made righteous, and Krishna has Arjuna proclaim that his devotee never perishes.</summary>
